patch_description: Crossover of the three programs. Key insight: the current program is the fastest (times_algorithm 0.01) thanks to vectorized packing, but its per-step greedy loop is still O(num_groups) iterations. The inspiration program's serpentine (snake) packing is fully vectorized in a single scatter — fastest of all. Meanwhile, the current/second program's replicate_experts gain formula (weight/logcnt) produced the better expert balancedness score (0.25 vs 0.24) compared to the weight/(cnt*(cnt+1)) marginal-gain formula. So the crossover takes: (1) serpentine vectorized balanced_packing from the inspiration program for maximum speed, and (2) the weight/logcnt greedy replication from the current program for the better expert balancedness, keeping everything else (hierarchical pipeline, inverse permutation, log2phy scatter) identical to the shared skeleton. This should keep balancedness at ~0.25/0.66 while minimizing algorithm execution time.
